claimsToVerify: Trenchers made of day-old or stale whole-meal bread were routinely used as plates and often distributed as alms.
Medieval nobility heavily used expensive imported spices (cinnamon, ginger, cloves, pepper) partly as a display of wealth.
Catholic dietary rules banned red meat on fast days, prompting consumption of fish, with beaver tails occasionally classified as fish due to their aquatic habitat.
